query: For high-entropy alloys in demanding engineering applications, what single testable hypothesis identifies an intervention that could improve resistance to thermally induced toughness loss, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an otherwise comparable baseline, defines the conditions under which it should hold, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies an experiment that could falsify it?

generation.hypothesis: Introducing refractory elements such as Ti, Zr, Hf, V, Nb, Ta, Cr, Mo, and W into high-entropy alloys (HEAs) can improve their resistance to thermally induced toughness loss.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloys (HEAs) with multiple principal elements
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of protective oxide scales, high thermal stability
generation.mechanism: Refractory elements enhance strength, hardness, and softening resistance at elevated temperatures
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved resistance to thermally induced toughness loss
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 800-1600 K, exposure time: >10^7 s
generation.uncertainty: Optimal composition and processing conditions for refractory HEAs

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of thermally induced toughness loss in refractory HEAs and conventional HEAs
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If refractory HEAs show no significant improvement in resistance to thermally induced toughness loss compared to conventional HEAs, the hypothesis is falsified.
